candidates.topic: The Radioactive Boy Scout — Teen Who Built a Nuclear Reactor in His Shed
candidates.teaser: A 17-year-old actually built a working nuclear reactor in his backyard — and nobody noticed for months.
candidates.video_title: Teen Built a Nuclear Reactor in His Shed
candidates.video_description: In 1994, David Hahn secretly assembled a neutron source in his Michigan shed using materials from household smoke detectors and camping lanterns. The EPA eventually declared his backyard a Superfund hazardous waste site. He was just 17.
candidates.script: A 17-year-old built a nuclear reactor in his garden shed — and it actually worked. David Hahn dismantled thousands of smoke detectors to extract americium-241, then stripped camping lanterns for thorium. By 1994, his backyard in Michigan was emitting radiation 1,000 times above safe levels. The EPA declared it a Superfund hazardous waste site. He never got a science fair trophy. He got a full hazmat cleanup. Was he a genius, a criminal, or just a kid who went too far?

candidates.topic: The Cotard Delusion — People Who Believe They Are Dead
candidates.teaser: Some people are completely convinced they are dead — and no amount of evidence can change their mind.
candidates.video_title: People Who Genuinely Believe They Are Dead
candidates.video_description: Cotard's Delusion is a rare neurological condition where patients sincerely believe they no longer exist — some stop eating because they feel corpses don't need food. The brain's emotional and facial recognition circuits disconnect, making the world feel utterly unreal.
candidates.script: Some people wake up one day completely convinced they are dead — and no doctor can talk them out of it. Cotard's Delusion is a real neurological condition where the brain's emotional recognition circuits disconnect from reality. Patients refuse to eat because, they argue, corpses don't need food. One man in 1880 insisted he had lost all his organs and his soul. Scans show their brains literally resemble those of people under anesthesia. So — if your brain stopped confirming you exist, would you believe anyone who said you do?

candidates.topic: The Feral Child of Aveyron — Boy Raised by the Wild
candidates.teaser: A boy emerged from a French forest in 1800 who had never spoken a word — and what scientists found next shattered everything about human language.
candidates.video_title: The Wild Boy Who Rewrote Human Language Science
candidates.video_description: In 1800, a naked boy emerged from the forests of Aveyron, France. He had lived alone in the wild for years, walked on all fours, felt no cold, and could not speak. His case became the first scientific study of feral children and exposed a critical window in human brain development that closes forever in early childhood.
candidates.script: A naked boy stumbled out of a French forest in 1800 and couldn't speak a single word — not one. Victor of Aveyron had spent years completely alone in the wild, feeling no cold, walking on all fours, eating raw food. Scientists rushed to teach him language. After years of intensive training, he learned almost nothing. Researchers realized there is a window in early childhood when the brain wires itself for language — and once it closes, it never reopens. Victor proved that being human isn't just biology. It has a deadline.

candidates.topic: The Time a Pilot Flew Inside a Tornado and Survived
candidates.teaser: One pilot accidentally flew his plane directly into a tornado — and what he saw inside defied everything meteorologists believed.
candidates.video_title: A Pilot Flew Inside a Tornado and Lived
candidates.video_description: In 1959, Marine pilot William Rankin ejected from his jet at 47,000 feet directly into a violent thunderstorm. He fell through the storm for 40 minutes instead of 13, pummeled by hail, lightning, and violent updrafts. He survived and gave scientists their first first-hand account of the inside of a severe storm.
candidates.script: A pilot ejected from his jet at 47,000 feet — directly into the heart of a violent thunderstorm. William Rankin's parachute should have delivered him to the ground in 13 minutes. Instead, violent updrafts kept hurling him back into the clouds for 40 minutes. Lightning struck within feet of him. Hail shredded his suit. He was nearly drowned in mid-air. He survived and gave meteorologists their first ever eyewitness account from inside a living storm. He described it as being trapped inside a white room that was trying to kill him.

candidates.topic: The Sleeping Sickness Epidemic — Encephalitis Lethargica 1920s
candidates.teaser: In the 1920s, a mysterious illness swept the world that left millions frozen — awake but completely unable to move — for decades.
candidates.video_title: The Disease That Froze a Million People Awake
candidates.video_description: Between 1915 and 1926, Encephalitis Lethargica infected over a million people worldwide, leaving thousands in a bizarre suspended state — conscious but motionless, frozen mid-sentence for years or even decades. Its cause has never been identified. Some patients were revived 40 years later by a new drug, only to lose that ability within months.
candidates.script: In 1920, people started freezing — mid-sentence, mid-step, eyes open, completely conscious but unable to move. Encephalitis Lethargica swept the world and left over a million people in a suspended state for years. Some sat motionless for four decades. Then in 1969, doctors gave them a new drug called L-DOPA and they woke up — remembered everything — like no time had passed. Most lost the effect within months and froze again. The disease has never been explained. Its cause remains completely unknown to this day.
